title: The spelling of Callender and of Haynesville
summary: Callender complains about people misspelling his name and spells out Bajan and Haynesville.

story.theme_name: How I got my name: nicknames and band monikers
story.community_name: How I got my name: nicknames and band names

blocks.x: Yeah. The difference in the Callenders would be in the spelling. Now, all of the Scotch descendants spelled the name Callender, the Irish descendants are Callendair. So that's why my name gets

screwed up so much in the spelling. I can write my name on something and give it somebody with the "e" real big on the end, and it will come back "Callendar." So I used to get real teed-off about it, but I guess I'm getting used to it now. So long as they call me, I don't care how they spell it.
And sometimes they don't get both "L's" in it, too.
I've seen it spelled like the calendar.
Yeah, they hear Callender, and they immediately think of a date "Calendar," and it's not like that at all.
Bajan. They say Bajin and it's spelled Bajan. That's a West Indian accent.
Haynesville. That's just a Post Office Box, and my grandfather's farm was just a few miles from there.
